title: 2012 HMMT February Guts Problem 1
statement: Square \(A B C D\) has side length 2 , and \(X\) is a point outside the square such that \(A X=X B=\sqrt{2}\). What is the length of the longest diagonal of pentagon \(A X B C D\) ?

solutions.text: \(\sqrt{10}\) Since \(A X=X B=\sqrt{2}\) and \(A B=2\), we have \(\angle A X B=90^{\circ}\). Hence, the distance from \(X\) to \(A B\) is 1 and the distance from \(X\) to \(C D\) is 3 . By inspection, the largest diagonals are thus \(B X=C X=\sqrt{3^{2}+1^{2}}\).
